thread:
maria: Heads up — discovered that the analytics-viewer role is able to read customer secrets (s3://customer-secrets) and decrypt with customer KMS key after the role-binding changes from yesterday's deploy. Not good.

alex: Wait, analytics-viewer was only supposed to have read-only access to internal analytics buckets. Can you paste the binding that changed?

maria: Pasted from authz-service logs:
```yaml
roleBinding: analytics-viewer
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: analytics-worker
    namespace: infra
resources:
  - arn:aws:s3:::customer-secrets/*
  - arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
verbs:
  - s3:GetObject
  - kms:Decrypt
```

jason: @oncall can you trigger emergency lockdown on the analytics-worker SA and block egress to S3/KMS? :lock: :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042, paging oncall.

claire: I just reverted the authz-service config in the cluster (rolled back commit 0f3c9a2). Removed the two customer resource ARNs from the binding. Patch applied to staging+prod.

security-bot: Audit scan found 18 accesses to customer-bucket by analytics-worker between 2026-03-20T02:14:05Z and 2026-03-20T02:22:11Z. Affected objects: 202 objects.

alex: Good rollback. Next steps: 1) disable analytics-worker tokens, 2) revoke temporary credentials, 3) rotate the CMK or re-encrypt sensitive objects, 4) run a quick diff of any data exfil.

maria: Commands I ran to lock down (prod):
```bash
# mark service account as suspended in authz DB
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://authz.internal/sa/infra/analytics-worker/suspend
# revoke short-term STS creds for role
aws sts revoke-session --session-id $(aws sts get-session-token --duration-seconds 3600 | jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken) || true
# add a deny policy to the S3 bucket policy for analytics-worker arn
```

jason: We've also disabled the roleMapping job that auto-promotes roles from the identity provider. PR #427 to remove the mapping rule is in progress.

claire: Evidence collection: I've exported CloudTrail events and put a copy into a forensics bucket (internal-only). Saved request IDs and principals.

security-bot: Collected artifacts: cloudtrail/2026/03/20/analytics-access-1945678901.json (sha256: e3b0c442...), authz/diffs/rollback-0f3c9a2.patch

alex: For the KMS key: recommendation is rotate and re-encrypt customer secrets with a new CMK, then schedule key-deletion window per policy. Also inform compliance + account teams.

maria: Notifying legal & CSMs. Starting key rotation runbook now. Will open a ticket with customers we think are impacted.

jason: After rollback and token revocation, run an allow-list scan for any downstream jobs referencing analytics-worker creds and rotate those too.

claire: ETA for initial containment: 27 minutes. Will follow up with timeline and list of affected customers.

maria: TL;DR — root cause: role-binding rule in yesterday's rollout included customer ARNs due to a templating bug in the roleMapping generator. Fix: tighter template validation, unit test for resource ARN filters, and an emergency gate for authz changes.

alex: Thanks everyone. After containment we should do a blameless postmortem and add an automated regression test to CI that verifies no customer ARNs end up in internal role bindings. :thumbsup:

jason: Agreed. Adding PM to follow-up.

maria: I'll update the incident ticket with all commands, logs, and timeline.

claire: Final note — rotated the STS keys for analytics-worker and set MFA enforcement for any role mapping changes.
